Dhaka Division has recorded the highest number of deaths linked to suspected measles, with 491 fatalities.

Sylhet Division follows with 192 deaths, while Chattogram has reported 100 deaths.

In the last 24 hours, 1,254 people sought hospital care for measles-like symptoms, and 1,032 were admitted.

The total number of hospital admissions for suspected measles has reached 189,484, with 181,756 patients recovered and discharged.

Since March 15, the DGHS has recorded 213,244 people with measles-like symptoms and 23,122 confirmed infections.

Health officials note that the exact number of infections is unknown as not all patients are tested, especially those who remain outside hospitals.

headline_marked: DMP [[probe into State Minister's display of firearms]] during anti-drug drive
headline: DMP probe into State Minister's display of firearms during anti-drug drive
summary: Dhaka Metropolitan Police have ordered an investigation after State Minister Ishraque Hossain brandished guns during a raid in Gandaria.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain and his associates for brandishing firearms during an 'anti-drug operation'.
The controversy began after the minister uploaded videos to his verified Facebook page showing him and another individual carrying firearms while chasing people in Gandaria.
In the videos, captioned 'Ishraque's action: Drug dens demolished, dealers handed over to police', the minister is seen actively participating in the raid.
DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the Deputy Commissioner of the DMP's Wari Division has been assigned to investigate the incident.
Shafiqul added that the DMP will take legal action if any violation of the law is found during the investigation.
When asked by journalists if a minister could perform police duties, the DB chief declined to comment.
caption:
A State Minister caught on camera brandishing a gun during a drug raid. Now, the police are investigating.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has ordered an investigation into State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain and his associates for brandishing firearms during an 'anti-drug operation'.

The controversy began after the minister uploaded videos to his verified Facebook page showing him and another individual carrying firearms while chasing people in Gandaria.

In the videos, captioned 'Ishraque's action: Drug dens demolished, dealers handed over to police', the minister is seen actively participating in the raid.

DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam stated that the Deputy Commissioner of the DMP's Wari Division has been assigned to investigate the incident.

Shafiqul added that the DMP will take legal action if any violation of the law is found during the investigation.

When asked by journalists if a minister could perform police duties, the DB chief declined to comment.

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star
